reported_snapshot.total_debt_note: Total indebtedness (principal) $47.5B ($46.9B carrying: $41.6B recourse, $5.3B non-recourse), up from $35.6B at 2026-06-30 and $21.6B at 2025-12-31. ~$11.0B of principal due in 2027. Weighted effective rate ~7.9%. Includes $7.7B of OEM (equipment-maker) financing. Plus $18.7B operating and $0.65B finance lease liabilities on balance sheet => ~$66.9B debt + leases.
reported_snapshot.cash_note: Cash & equivalents $4.12B plus $2.28B restricted cash ($6.4B total); $5.7B undrawn facility capacity; total liquidity ~$9.8B.
reported_snapshot.fcf_note: Q3 OCF $1.975B less cash purchases of PP&E $9.441B (cash-flow statement). Company-defined capex (incl. some leased/vendor-financed equipment) was $14.5B. TTM OCF $7.2B vs TTM PP&E purchases $27.6B.
reported_snapshot.capex_guidance: FY2026 capex $37-39B (low end raised from $35B); 2027 capex roughly in line with 2026 if only committed backlog is served.
reported_snapshot.rpo_note: Revenue backlog ~$132.5B (RPO $132.3B per 10-Q), up from ~$104B at 2026-06-30; ~36% expected within 24 months. >50% of backlog tied to one contract with delivery starting by end-2026.
reported_snapshot.other: Q3 revenue $3.661B (+168% y/y); net loss $709M; interest expense $846M vs GAAP operating income $207M; Q4 interest guided $1.05-1.15B; FY26 revenue guide $13.0-13.3B; adj. EBITDA $2.26B. Stockholders' equity ~$4.0B.

off_balance_items.description: Executed leases (primarily data centers, equipment, offices) not yet commenced; estimated future undiscounted payments; commence 2026-2029, terms 7-17 years. Up from $35.5B at June 30 and $38.5B at Dec 31, 2025.
off_balance_items.counterparty: Data-center landlords/developers (not named; includes AMD-related leases ~530 MW signed July 2026)

off_balance_items.description: Single-site data-center lease (453 MW delivered in phases 2026-2028) with rent capped at $16.9B over ~16 years; payments depend on landlord construction cost and are excluded from the $47.4B figure.
off_balance_items.source_title: CoreWeave 10-Q Q3 2026, via sec-api.io / Filing Insights

off_balance_items.description: Committed future data-center construction costs ($2.1B) plus ~$4B of other enforceable purchase commitments (technology equipment, software/services). Separately ~$4.5B of equipment purchases sat in accrued liabilities (on balance sheet).
off_balance_items.source_title: CoreWeave 10-Q Q3 2026 contractual obligations (listed.markets); Filing Insights

off_balance_items.description: Unconsolidated VIEs/joint ventures: maximum exposure to loss ~$1.9B (JV) plus a VIE-lessor lease with $1.2B committed payments (already within lease figures). DDTL 5.0/5.5 SPV loans carry unconditional parent guarantees (on balance sheet).

Nvidia (key/sole GPU supplier) bought $2.0B of CoreWeave stock in Jan 2026 (22.9M shares at $87.20) and holds roughly 10-11%; CoreWeave spends most of its $37-39B capex on Nvidia systems. CoreWeave is the RECIPIENT of this vendor support.
off_balance_items.source_title: Yahoo Finance: Nvidia is CoreWeave's key sole supplier and $6.3B backstop

off_balance_items.description: Nvidia capacity backstop: Sept 2025 order (initial value $6.3B) obliging Nvidia to buy CoreWeave's residual unsold capacity through 2032-04-13, subject to delivery/service conditions and termination for breach or insolvency. Supports lender confidence; worth ~$1B/yr vs ~$3.4B+/yr interest run-rate. Nvidia interim CEO said (Nov 2026) it will be more selective on future guarantees; existing commitments unchanged.
off_balance_items.source_title: Yahoo Finance: 'Stay away from CoreWeave' - Huang scandal puts Nvidia's $6.3B backstop in focus

off_balance_items.description: OEM/equipment-maker financing ($6.9B recourse + $0.8B non-recourse) - suppliers lending CoreWeave money to buy their servers; $1.5B of equipment payables were converted into OEM debt in 9M 2026 without cash moving. On balance sheet as debt (not added to off-balance total).
off_balance_items.counterparty: Server OEMs (e.g., Dell) - not individually named

off_balance_items.description: Two unnamed customers were 30% and 24% of Q3 revenue (top customer 67% a year earlier; Microsoft was 67% of FY2025 revenue). Named commitments: OpenAI up to ~$22.4B cumulative (latest order $6.5B through May 2031), Meta ~$14.2B (to Dec 2031) + ~$21.0B (to Dec 2032), Jane Street ~$6B. >50% of backlog tied to a single contract. OpenAI is itself vendor-financed (Nvidia equity).
off_balance_items.source_title: CoreWeave 10-Q Q3 2026 risk factors (listed.markets); Inside Deep Tech

off_balance_items.description: Nvidia is supplier, shareholder, customer (renting capacity) and backstop for CoreWeave, and also an equity investor in OpenAI, a CoreWeave customer. Nvidia equity/backstop -> CoreWeave borrows against GPUs -> buys more Nvidia GPUs.

Expected ~$9B of customer prepayments/deposits over the following three months (>$3B tied to recontracting paid-off infrastructure). Funds capex but creates a delivery obligation; converts financing risk into execution risk.
off_balance_items.source_title: TechTimes: CoreWeave Q3 - $9B customer prepayments expected

total_note: Hard, quantified obligations not on the balance sheet: $47.4B leases not yet commenced + up to $16.9B single-site capped lease + $2.1B construction commitments + ~$4.0B other purchase commitments + $1.9B JV max loss exposure = ~$72.3B. Excludes Nvidia's $6.3B backstop (an asset/support for CoreWeave, not an obligation), Nvidia's $2B equity, OEM financing (already in debt), prepayments (future liabilities), and backlog/customer commitments (revenue, not obligations). Adding on-balance debt ($47.5B) and lease liabilities ($19.3B), total fixed obligations ~$139B vs TTM operating cash flow ~$7.2B (~19x) and equity ~$4B.

credit_signals.detail: Moody's Ba3 corporate family, B1 senior unsecured (stable), affirmed 2026-10-20. S&P B+ issuer; B on 9.625% 2032 notes. Fitch issuer BB- (positive outlook, July 2026). Contract-backed DDTL 4.0 rated A3 (Moody's) / A(low) DBRS; DDTL 5.0/5.5 Ba2 / BB+.
5-year CDS rose as much as 76bp to 1,232.6bp on Nov 20 (implies >65% 5-yr default probability); Deutsche Bank data showed >1,289bp on Nov 19; ~1,140bp after the midterms.

Unsecured notes (coupons 8.5-9.75%) trading ~80 cents: 9.75% 2031 at 79.75 (15.83% yield) on Nov 2; 9.625% 2032 yield >16% on Nov 6, 14.21% on Nov 11. CEO: will not use unsecured market at current yields.

$4.2B 2.875% convertible senior notes due 2033 closed Sept 22, 2026 (conversion ~$97.85). DDTL 5.5 $2.6B at SOFR+5.50% (Aug 2026, $1.56B drawn). Seeking >= $4B investment-grade loan backed by Meta contracts via Morgan Stanley/MUFG at ~7-7.5% (Nov 2026, not closed).
ATM program for up to 35M Class A shares (with collared forwards) set up Sept 17, 2026.
Q3 net interest expense $846M (4x GAAP operating income of $207M); Q4 guided $1.05-1.15B.

news_context.headline_summary: CoreWeave shares fall 15.5% in a day; unsecured bond yields hit ~15-16%, CDS >1,000bp amid rumors about debt and financing access (later cited in 10-Q risk factors).
news_context.why_it_matters: Unsecured funding window effectively closed; company now depends on asset-backed loans, converts, prepayments and equity.

news_context.headline_summary: Microsoft capex $45.2B misses, citing delayed third-party capacity deliveries; trims CY2026 capex to ~$170B; neoclouds sell off.
news_context.why_it_matters: Microsoft was 67% of CoreWeave's 2025 revenue; delivery delays defer revenue while interest keeps accruing.

news_context.headline_summary: Democratic midterm sweep and 41 local data-center ballot measures; CoreWeave -9%, CDS ~1,140bp.
news_context.why_it_matters: Political/permitting backlash slows new capacity, hitting the most leveraged builders first.

news_context.headline_summary: Microsoft shrinking its roster of neocloud partners and prioritizing own data centers (CNBC/Bloomberg); also winds down Oracle rental deal.
news_context.why_it_matters: Key anchor customer reducing third-party reliance raises renewal and concentration risk for CoreWeave's backlog.

news_context.headline_summary: Q3 beat: revenue $3.66B (+168%), backlog $132.5B, FY guide raised; but net loss $709M, interest $846M, capex $14.5B, debt $47.5B; ~$9B prepayments expected.
news_context.why_it_matters: Strong demand but growth is almost entirely debt- and prepayment-funded; interest cost exceeds operating profit.

news_context.headline_summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; interim CEO Kress says Nvidia will be more selective on future investments and guarantees, existing neocloud commitments unchanged.
news_context.why_it_matters: Nvidia is CoreWeave's supplier, ~10% shareholder and $6.3B capacity backstop; perceived support is central to lender confidence.

news_context.headline_summary: CoreWeave marketing >= $4B Meta-contract-backed IG loan at ~7.5% vs ~16% on its unsecured bonds.
news_context.why_it_matters: Lenders underwrite CoreWeave's customers, not CoreWeave; access depends on keeping AA-rated customer contracts.

news_context.headline_summary: CoreWeave CDS widens to ~1,233bp as AI selloff spreads to credit.
news_context.why_it_matters: Market prices a majority chance of default within five years.

hidden_leverage_assessment.rationale: CoreWeave already owes about $47.5B of debt plus $19B of booked leases, and on top of that has ~$72B of signed obligations that are not on its balance sheet yet (mostly data-center leases starting 2026-2029). That is many times its ~$7B of yearly operating cash flow and ~$4B of equity, and its interest bill alone is bigger than its operating profit. It survives by continuously raising new money - GPU-backed loans, convertibles, share sales and customer prepayments - and lenders mainly trust the contracts of a few giant customers (Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta), one of which (OpenAI) is itself funded partly by Nvidia. Nvidia's $2B stock purchase and $6.3B 'buy unsold capacity' backstop make the loop look safer, but they are small relative to the obligations, and bond and CDS markets (~16% yields, ~1,200bp CDS) are pricing real default risk.
hidden_leverage_assessment.biggest_hidden_risk: If a top customer (e.g., Microsoft consolidating neoclouds) cuts or delays capacity while credit markets stay shut, CoreWeave is still on the hook for ~$64B of signed, mostly long-dated leases with no cash cushion to cover them.
hidden_leverage_assessment.what_would_change_my_mind: Several quarters of positive free cash flow plus investment-grade asset loans closing at ~7% with backlog diversifying away from Microsoft/OpenAI/Meta and CDS falling well below 500bp.
